### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 30a8047bad6e264762dd41ded7f1290c1224afc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · head 1e46a685be · card #37917 · area s2-eval · 2026-11-27T15:56Z

**L1 checklist** (no review face on this file list: this record is the review of record)
- **Shape and checks.** 35 success, 21 expected skip, 0 failed on the head (Test Core 10/10, Check Changeset success). 75 changed lines: two committed builds' provenance, one build, the scenarios README, and a test; not governed. `skip-changeset` is right: the package change is a test, outside the published `files[]`.
- **Which side is right: the scorer.** The card asks for claim lines "edited inline on the claim's form". The build was authored on 2026-11-18, when `inlineEdit` on a master-detail FK inlined the child by itself; since the #35889 ruling (ADR-0035 as amended 2026-11-20) a child is inlined only where a field group of the master names it, and #37135's check reads that. So on today's tree the unamended build does not do what the card asks, and the check's "0 edited inline" is true. No product call is made here: the runtime rule was ruled, and the card is unchanged.
- **The fix.** One field group `lines` (`relatedList: "demotravel_claim_line"`) on the claim, nothing else; the provenance records it as an `amended` entry with the sha256 it replaced, and the new `scored` block names the runner, date and Build reading (141/141, was 140/141); `verified` keeps the authoring run's 135/135. `order_to_cash` gets its `scored` (174/174) too. The README says when a scorer change re-scores a build and who moves `scored`.
- **The new pin.** `verified-builds.test.ts` scores every committed build against its namespaced card with this tree's scorer and requires every Build check to pass with no roll-up charge, so the next scorer change that refuses a build fails in its own PR.
- **Effect on rounds.** The ask-day round installs this build with `--template`; ask turns do not score Build, and no new round is run (rounds paused 11-27). A later ask round on the amended build differs from the #34996 rounds by this one field group, which the provenance names.
- **Declarations.** `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. `Fixes #37917` is right: both items are done.
